name: Cut bar stock to length on the horizontal band saw

working.role: works the saw: the feed selector and rate knob, the bow, the vise, Start and coolant

steadying.role: feeds the bar to the work stop and holds it down on the bed against the fixed jaw until the vise bites; off the saw while it cuts; lifts the cut piece away

phases.what: The working hand to the feed selector
Turn the feed selector to O, so the hydraulic cylinder holds the bow wherever it is lifted to [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
Lift the bow by the blade tension handle, the JET's lifting point, where its bow weighs 18-20 lb [proposed: duration_s, the 25 mm clearance]
phases.ends_on: the blade about 25 mm above where the bar will lie

phases.what: Set the descent rate for the material: counterclockwise opens the valve and feeds faster [proposed: force_n, turns, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the knob at the shop's mark for the material

phases.what: Fingers hooked under the rack block lift it, and the palm slides the floating jaw open past the bar's width [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the jaw clear of the bar

phases.what: Both hands slide the bar along the bed between the jaws, the cut-off length past the blade, until its end meets the work stop [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the bar's end touches the work stop

phases.what: The steadying hand holds the bar down on the bed and against the fixed jaw, about 20 N; the working hand slides the floating jaw up to the bar and lets the rack block drop back into the rack [proposed: force_n, the 20 N hold, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the jaw touches the bar and the block drops into the rack

phases.what: Turn the vise handwheel to clamp; the steadying hand stays on the bar until the jaw bites [proposed: force_n, turns, duration_s, the end condition]
phases.ends_on: snug: the steadying hand can no longer slide or roll the bar

phases.what: Both hands off the bar: the working hand to Start, the steadying hand back to the side, clear of the blade
Press Start with the bow still up: the blade must reach full speed before it meets the work [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the blade running at full speed

phases.what: Coolant switch to I, for steel [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
Feed selector to I: the bow comes down under its own weight at the set rate [proposed: force_n, duration_s]

Hands off the saw and away from the blade while it cuts; watch the chips: slightly curled and silvery is right, powdery means too light a feed or a dull blade, blue or straw-coloured means feed or speed too high [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the blade stops itself at the end of the cut (the limit switch)

phases.what: The steadying hand to the cut piece, keeping clear of the blade
Lift the cut piece off the bed, away from the blade area, and set it down on the bench [proposed: duration_s]

sources.ref: JET (JPW Industries), HBS-916 / HBS-1018 Horizontal Band Saw, Operating Instructions and Parts Manual M-414468, rev. I (2019): safety rules 10-12, §7.8 bow weight, §7.9 vise, §7.10 work stop, §7.11 limit switch, §8 controls, §10 operation, §10.3 chips
sources.gives: the order (feed off, raise the bow, set the rate, clamp, Start, coolant, feed on, the saw stops itself); the quick-release vise (lift the rack block, slide the jaw, drop the block, turn the handwheel); the bow weighs 18-20 lb at the tension handle; the blade at full speed before it touches the work; hands away from the blade, also when removing the cut piece; reading the chips

sources.ref: McMaster-Carr 8962N13, 9 x 16 in horizontal band saw (asset record bandsaw)
sources.gives: the saw modelled: quick-release vise, manual or automatic feed

sources.ref: Kurt, 'Double Station Manual Vise Setup' (YouTube), measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker; borrowed, as no footage of this tool was tracked
sources.gives: reach durations: the right hand's interquartile range, 0.32-0.67 s

notes: Written from JET's HBS-916 manual. McMaster sells 8962N13 without naming its maker or publishing a manual, and its blade (131-1/2 in) and speeds (98-262 sfpm) match no 9 x 16 saw found, so the JET, a 9 x 16 saw with the same controls (hydraulic feed valve and on/off selector, quick-release vise, limit switch), stands in for the order of work and the bow's weight. The left blade guide bracket (JET §10, step 3) is set once per bar size, so it is left out. Grasps are this card's reading of the controls; the maker names none. Proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): #2, #11, #12 2 N and 0.5 s to turn a selector or switch, no source gives either; #3 the 80-89 N is the JET's bow, borrowed because McMaster gives no bow weight for 8962N13, and the 1.2 s lift and 25 mm clearance are guesses; #4 2 N, a quarter turn and 0.8 s on the rate knob, the setting depends on the material; #5 10 N and 1.0 s to slide the jaw, unmeasured; #6 15 N, about 0.2 friction on a 7 kg bar, and 2.0 s; #7 10 N on the jaw, 20 N holding the bar, 1.0 s; #8 40 N at the handwheel rim, half a turn and 1.5 s, and 'snug' as the end, none of which the manual states; #10 5 N, matching the VF-2 station's proposed button force, and 0.3 s; #13 1-3 minutes, which depends on the bar's section and material; #15 1.5 s.
